(1) that

$S_{\mu}=\{x\in\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}\mid\eta(a)\cdot x\to L_{\mu}\text{ when $a\to 0$}\}.$

Therefore $X$ meets $S_{\mu}$ if and only if $L_{\mu}\in X$, whence

$X\subset\bigcup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mu\in X_{*}(T)\\
L_{\mu}\in X\end{subarray}}S_{\mu},$

and therefore

$X\subset\bigcup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\mu\in X_{*}(T)\\
L_{\mu}\in X\end{subarray}}\bigl(\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}\cap S_{\mu}\bigr).$

The corollary now follows from Theorem 5.2(2). ∎

The following theorem is the analogue of Theorem 5.2 for the Borel subgroup $B^{-}$ in place of  $B$.
card.label: Theorem 5.2

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
